context.question: If I should purchase Master B. his houses — shall I deal with the seller and procure money in time to pay for the purchase?
context.asked_at: 31 March 1634, 6 p.m. (figure heading as printed: '31 March 1634. 6 Hor. P.M.')
context.setting: In 1634 the inheritance of the house he lived in (in the Strand, London) and others were offered to him for sale; his own money could not be called in for six months; the seller's first demand was £530

attachments.key_positions: Sun (significator of the seller) locally placed in the 7th, received by Venus(?) in exaltation near the cusp of the 7th; lord of the 7th also lord of the 11th (Lilly's hopes); Venus applying to a trine of Saturn, lord of the 4th (the houses); Moon translating light by square aspect out of signs of long ascension; Mercury, lord of Lilly's 2nd, retrograde; Saturn lord of the 4th without material debilities except retrogradation and cadency
attachments.note: The ascending sign/degree is garbled in the 1647 OCR ('the degree of the Sign is the same wherein [Mars] was in my Radix'); positions above are those Lilly names in prose.

provenance.book: William Lilly, Christian Astrology (1647), Book II
